description: This file defines the 'RealDistribution' interface in the Apache Commons Math library, outlining methods for probability functions, distribution properties, and sampling related to real-valued statistical distributions.

classes.name: RealDistribution
classes.description: Interface for real-valued probability distributions, providing methods for probability calculation, density, cumulative functions, quantiles, and sampling.

methods.name: probability
methods.description: Returns the probability mass at a specific point (for discrete distributions).

methods.name: density
methods.description: Returns the probability density at a specific point.

methods.name: cumulativeProbability
methods.description: Returns the cumulative probability up to a given point.

methods.name: cumulativeProbability (x0, x1)
methods.description: Returns the probability between two points (deprecated, to be renamed in future versions).

methods.name: inverseCumulativeProbability
methods.description: Returns the quantile for a given probability.

methods.name: getNumericalMean
methods.description: Returns the mean of the distribution.

methods.name: getNumericalVariance
methods.description: Returns the variance of the distribution.

methods.name: getSupportLowerBound
methods.description: Returns the lower bound of the distribution's support.

methods.name: getSupportUpperBound
methods.description: Returns the upper bound of the distribution's support.

methods.name: isSupportLowerBoundInclusive
methods.description: Indicates if the support lower bound is inclusive (deprecated).

methods.name: isSupportUpperBoundInclusive
methods.description: Indicates if the support upper bound is inclusive (deprecated).

methods.name: isSupportConnected
methods.description: Indicates whether the support is a connected interval.

methods.name: reseedRandomGenerator
methods.description: Reseeds the distribution's internal random number generator.

methods.name: sample (int sampleSize)
methods.description: Generates an array of random samples of specified size.
